metadata.title: PANW Stock Slips After-Hours On Former Executive’s Accounting Fraud Allegations: Firm Denies Claims

content.text:
McGill claims senior leadership endorsed practices that artificially boosted revenue by pushing resellers to issue purchase orders before customers had formally approved the deals.
He says he objected to these efforts and was later terminated after the company fabricated a story about an altercation with a competitor's employee as the reason for his dismissal.
Palo Alto spokesperson Allie Cefalo told Bloomberg the allegations from "a disgruntled former employee are completely meritless."
Shares of Palo Alto Networks (PANW) fell sharply in after-hours trading on Wednesday after reports that a former regional vice president has sued the cybersecurity company, alleging he was fired for raising concerns about accounting practices intended to inflate revenue.
The stock, which closed the regular session modestly higher, dropped roughly 5% in extended trading. The move erased much of the gains the shares had built in recent days on strong quarterly results and a major acquisition announcement.
According to Bloomberg, Dan McGill filed a complaint in federal court in Manhattan on Friday. He claims senior leadership endorsed practices that artificially boosted revenue by pushing resellers to issue purchase orders before customers had formally approved the deals. McGill, a former regional vice president, said he objected to these efforts and was later terminated. He alleged that the company fabricated a story about an altercation with a competitor's employee as the reason for his dismissal.
In the complaint, McGill specifically alleges two examples involving his then-supervisor Darren Estridge. In July 2023, he says Estridge directed a value-added reseller to issue a roughly $4 million purchase order for a Fire Department of New York deal without the customer's knowledge or approval so the revenue could be booked before the fiscal year ended on July 31; the actual customer order came later in August.
In April 2024, McGill claims Estridge pushed another reseller to pre-issue an order for a multi-year New York State deal of about $5 million that was booked for the quarter ending April 30, again without a proper customer purchase order.
Palo Alto Networks rejected the claims. Spokesperson Allie Cefalo said in a statement to Stocktwits that the allegations from "a disgruntled former employee are completely meritless."
"We will use the appropriate legal means to defend the company against these baseless claims," she added.
The lawsuit comes just days after Palo Alto reported strong fiscal first-quarter 2027 results and announced a $4.5 billion all-stock acquisition of Applied Compute, a platform for post-training and inference of open-weight AI models. The deal, expected to close in the fiscal third quarter of 2027, is part of Palo Alto's push to expand into securing enterprise AI.
For the quarter ended October 31, Palo Alto's revenue rose 39% year over year to $3.44 billion, and earnings were $1.05 per share. On the same day, the company raised its full-year fiscal 2027 outlook, which excludes any contribution from the pending acquisition. The company now expects revenue of $14.52 billion–$14.57 billion, marking 26–27% growth, from the prior range of $14.10 billion–$14.20 billion, and an earnings range of $4.26–$4.30 from $4.16–$4.19.
The company had previously flagged margin pressure in its fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 results and earnings call in early September. Chief Financial Officer Dipak Golechha said at the time that the shift toward more cloud-based software was expected to drive hosting costs higher than total revenue in fiscal 2027, contributing to pressure on gross margins. He reiterated the point on the November 18 call while noting that elevated hardware component costs and product-mix effects continued to weigh on margins in the near to medium term.
How Did PANW Retail Traders React?
On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around PANW stock fell from 'extremely bullish' to 'bullish' territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume fell from 'extremely high' to 'high' levels.
A Stocktwits user opined that the stock should be down further over the allegations.
Another user dismissed the lawsuit as a move by a disgruntled former employee.
